title: 10. Exercises: AsyncIO Synchronization
summary: Next: 11_asyncio_advanced.md — Advanced asyncio patterns and techniques →
objectives: Solve the AsyncIO Synchronization exercises without looking at the lesson
Test edge cases and explain your approach

sections.title: Exercises
sections.body:
### Exercise 1: Rate Limiter

Create a rate limiter that:

1. Allows max N requests per second
2. Uses Semaphore for limiting
3. Tracks and reports actual rate

### Exercise 2: Read-Write Lock

Implement async read-write lock:

1. Multiple readers allowed
2. Only one writer at a time
3. Writers have priority

### Exercise 3: Resource Pool

Create a resource pool:

1. Fixed number of resources
2. Check-out and check-in
3. Timeout on checkout

### Exercise 4: Barrier with Timeout

Implement barrier with timeout:

1. Tasks wait at barrier
2. If timeout, release anyway
3. Report which tasks timed out

### Exercise 5: Async Queue with Priorities

Extend priority queue:

1. Multiple priority levels
2. Fair scheduling within level
3. Starvation prevention

### Exercise 6: Latch

Implement countdown latch:

1. Initialize with count
2. count_down() decrements
3. wait() blocks until zero

### Exercise 7: Async Mutex with Timeout

Create a lock with timeout:

1. acquire(timeout) method
2. Returns True/False
3. Proper cleanup on timeout

### Exercise 8: Event Bus

Create async event bus:

1. Subscribe to events
2. Publish events
3. Async handlers

### Exercise 9: Bounded Buffer

Create bounded buffer:

1. Max size limit
2. Block on full/empty
3. Support timeout

### Exercise 10: Async Monitor

Create a monitor pattern:

1. Combines lock and conditions
2. Multiple named conditions
3. Wait/notify on each
